newsitem.title: INDIA: Two bombs injure at least 10 in Delhi - police.
newsitem.headline: Two bombs injure at least 10 in Delhi - police.

text.p: Two bombs, one in a bus and the other in a jeep, exploded in the Indian capital on Saturday, injuring at least 10 people, police said.
A police spokesman said no deaths were reported in the blasts, which occurred minutes apart in the Samaipur Badli area in the northwestern area of Delhi.
No one had so far claimed responsibility for the blasts, spokesman Kamal Singh said.
United News of India (UNI) said five passengers of the jeep were in critical condition in a local hospital.
The news agency said the first bomb exploded in the state-owned bus at around 5:15 p.m. (1145 GMT). The second rocked the jeep minutes later some 500 metres (yards) away.

It was not known how many passengers in the bus were injured. Earlier, police had said 10 people were hurt in the bus, which was travelling from New Delhi to Sonepat in neighbouring Haryana state. Later they said the injured included passengers from the jeep.
UNI had reported earlier on Saturday that a bomb went off in the morning in a house in south Delhi, injuring one person. But police later said the explosion did not involve a bomb.
At least 31 people were killed in three separate bomb attacks in the capital over the past year. Police suspected Kashmiri or Sikh militants for carrying out the attacks.
